faq.q: What is the best time of year for calm seas in Marbella?
faq.a: From May to October, the Mediterranean is typically calm, with sea temperatures between 18°C and 24°C. July and August offer the most stable conditions, with light winds and minimal swell. Spring and autumn can still be excellent, but you may encounter occasional easterly winds (Levante) that create choppier seas.

faq.q: How do I check the Marbella sea conditions forecast before my boat rental?
faq.a: Use marine forecast sites like Windguru or Windy, and look at the local AEMET (Spanish met office) forecast for the Costa del Sol. Pay attention to wind speed (kts), wave height (m), and swell period. For a reliable day on the water, aim for winds under 15 kts and waves under 1m.

faq.q: What wind speed is too high for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Generally, winds above 20 kts make conditions uncomfortable, especially for smaller boats like the Mariah SX21 or Speedboat. Our licensed skippers monitor the forecast and will advise if a charter should be rescheduled for safety. If the forecast shows gusts over 25 kts, it's best to postpone.

faq.q: Does the sea state affect which boat I can rent?
faq.a: Yes. Larger vessels like the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Ferretti 94 (29m) handle rougher seas better than a 6.4m speedboat. On days with a moderate swell, we recommend a flybridge or yacht for stability. Our team will help you choose the right boat based on the forecast and your group size.

faq.q: What is the water temperature in Marbella in summer?
faq.a: In July and August, the sea temperature averages 22–24°C, perfect for swimming and water toys. June and September are slightly cooler at around 20–21°C. Even in early summer, you can comfortably enjoy a dip, especially if you're anchored in a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro.

faq.q: Can I reschedule my boat rental if the forecast is bad?
faq.a: Yes, we understand weather can change. If the forecast shows unsafe conditions, we'll work with you to reschedule to a better day or offer a refund. Our skippers have the final say on the day, and your safety is always the priority. Contact us via WhatsApp to discuss options.

faq.q: What does 'Levante' wind mean for Marbella boat trips?
faq.a: Levante is an easterly wind that can blow from the Mediterranean, bringing choppier seas and sometimes overcast skies. It's most common in spring and autumn. When Levante is strong, the sea state can be rough, especially near the coast. Our skippers know the best sheltered routes, like heading towards Cabopino or Estepona.

data.body_html:
Planning a boat rental in Marbella? The difference between a perfect day on the water and a bumpy one often comes down to the Marbella sea conditions forecast. Wind, waves, and swell can change quickly along the Costa del Sol, so knowing what to look for — and how to plan around it — ensures your charter is smooth, safe, and unforgettable. Here's your practical guide to reading the forecast before you step aboard in Puerto Banús.

Why the Marbella Sea Conditions Forecast Matters

The Mediterranean isn't always a millpond. Even in summer, a thermal breeze can pick up by midday, creating a short chop that makes smaller boats feel lively. Checking the forecast isn't about being cautious — it's about choosing the right boat and the right route. For example, a Mangusta 80 (24m) will glide through conditions that might make a Mariah SX21 (6.4m) feel uncomfortable. Our skippers are experts at reading the sea, but you'll enjoy your day far more if you have realistic expectations from the start.

Key Forecast Terms You Need to Know

When you open a marine forecast, you'll see three numbers that matter:

  • Wind speed (kts): Under 10 kts = calm; 10–15 kts = pleasant; 15–20 kts = choppy; 20+ kts = rough.
  • Wave height (m): Under 0.5m = flat; 0.5–1m = slight; 1–2m = moderate; 2m+ = rough.
  • Swell period (s): Longer periods (10s+) mean smoother, rolling swell; shorter periods mean steep, choppy waves.

For a comfortable day on a 12m boat like the Astondoa 40, aim for wind below 15 kts and waves under 1m. If the forecast shows more, you can still go out — but you might prefer a larger yacht or a sheltered itinerary.

Typical Sea State by Season in Marbella

SeasonSea temp (°C)Wind (typical)Wave heightBest for
Spring (Mar–May)15–18Light–moderate, occasional Levante0.5–1.5mLarger yachts, sightseeing
Summer (Jun–Aug)20–24Light–moderate, sea breeze afternoon0.3–1mAll boats, swimming, water toys
Autumn (Sep–Nov)18–22Variable, possible storms0.5–1.5mFlybridges, catamarans
Winter (Dec–Feb)14–16Stronger winds, rougher seas1–2mOnly large yachts, rare

As you can see, summer offers the most predictable conditions. But even in July, an afternoon easterly breeze can create a chop near the coast. That's why we recommend morning departures — the sea is often glassy until 11:00.

How to Use the Forecast to Choose Your Boat

If the forecast shows calm conditions (wind <10 kts, waves <0.5m), any boat in our fleet is a good option. For a small group, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is perfect for a quick spin along the coast. If there's a moderate chop, step up to a Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) or a Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) — the flybridge offers a smoother ride and panoramic views. For rougher days, the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94 (29m) will keep you comfortable even in 1.5m seas.

Where to Check the Forecast: Our Go-To Sources

We use a combination of tools to plan our charters:

  • Windguru / Windy: These apps give you wind speed, gust, and wave height for the exact coordinates of Puerto Banús.
  • AEMET (Spanish Met Office): The official marine forecast for the Costa del Sol, updated several times daily.
  • Buoy data: The nearest deep-water buoy (off Málaga) provides real-time wave height and period.

We recommend checking the forecast 24 hours before your rental, and again on the morning of. Conditions can change, but the trend is usually reliable. Our skippers also do a final assessment before departure.

What Happens If the Forecast Is Bad?

If the forecast shows unsafe conditions (wind >25 kts, waves >2m), we'll contact you to reschedule or offer a full refund. We want you to have a great day, not a scary one. In most cases, we can suggest an alternative day or a different boat that handles better. For example, a catamaran like the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax) is more stable than a monohull, so it's a good fallback on slightly choppy days.

Local Knowledge: Sheltered Routes When It's Breezy

Even on days with moderate wind, there are sheltered spots along the coast. If the east wind (Levante) is blowing, we head west towards Cabopino or Estepona, where the cliffs and coves offer protection. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are two of our favourite anchorages — they're usually calm even when the open sea is choppy. Our skippers know these spots intimately, so you'll still get a fantastic trip.

Plan Your Charter with Confidence

Now that you know how to read the Marbella sea conditions forecast, you're ready to book. All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance — so you can focus on enjoying the sea. For a transparent quote on any of our boats, browse the full fleet or contact us via WhatsApp. We'll help you pick the perfect boat for the conditions and your group.
